papers.title: Risk-aware hybrid reinforcement learning and robust optimization for reliable PV-battery scheduling under uncertainty
papers.abstract: Abstract The increasing penetration of photovoltaic (PV) generation and battery energy storage systems (BESSs) has intensified the need for intelligent scheduling strategies that can simultaneously reduce operating cost, preserve battery health, and ensure operational reliability under significant uncertainty. In practical grid-connected PV–battery systems, the stochastic nature of solar power, load demand, and electricity prices often leads to constraint violations and high tail-risk costs when conventional optimization or purely data-driven methods are used. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a risk-sensitive hybrid framework that integrates Soft Actor-Critic (SAC), Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR), conformal uncertainty estimation (CUE), and robust optimization (RO) in a unified energy management architecture. The SAC agent learns a stochastic dispatch policy, while CVaR explicitly penalizes unfavorable cost outcomes and CUE provides distribution-free uncertainty bounds for uncertain inputs. These bounds are then embedded into a robust optimization layer to guarantee feasibility under adverse operating conditions. In addition, an adaptive fusion mechanism combines the outputs of the learning-based and robust controllers to balance economic performance and reliability. Simulation results for a typical residential PV–battery system demonstrate that the proposed method achieves the best trade-off among cost, risk, and constraint satisfaction. Compared with a rule-based baseline, the full model reduces the SOC violation rate from 4.8% to below 1%, while also lowering the total operating cost and CVaR. Moreover, the proposed framework outperforms the RO-only variant by achieving a lower average cost without sacrificing robustness, and it consistently provides the highest reliability across independent runs. These results confirm that the proposed hybrid approach offers a practical and scalable solution for secure and economical PV–battery scheduling under uncertainty.

papers.title: World-model-inspired latent action priors for home energy optimization
papers.abstract: The integration of renewable energy sources into residential microgrids introduces operational challenges associated with intermittency, electricity-price volatility, and the progressive degradation of battery storage systems. Reinforcement learning has emerged as a promising approach for battery scheduling, yet many existing methods remain vulnerable to actions that fall outside the support of the training data and often generalize poorly across operating regimes. This work proposes an offline reinforcement learning framework that combines a conditional variational autoencoder with latent action priors in order to constrain policy optimization to a structured latent action space learned from expert demonstrations generated by entropy-regularized and deterministic actor-critic controllers. The proposed methodology consists of three stages: first, learning a latent representation of admissible battery actions from expert trajectories through a conditional variational autoencoder; second, extracting an offline policy within the learned latent manifold through implicit value-based policy improvement; and third, deploying an out-of-distribution detection mechanism that gradually blends the learned controller with a conservative fallback policy under distributional uncertainty. Experiments on the GEFCom2014 benchmark, the StoreNet House 4 scenario, and the CityLearn environment show that the proposed method achieves the highest daily net benefit among value-based and offline controllers, with improvements of up to 61.9% over deep Q-learning and 7.9% over standard model predictive control on GEFCom2014. In addition, the method converges substantially faster than competing baselines, requiring up to nine times less training time in CityLearn. At the same time, the results show that the approach does not uniformly dominate all references: in the policy-based comparison on CityLearn, deep deterministic policy gradients achieve a lower monetary cost, and in standard continuous-control benchmarks, proximal policy optimization and twin delayed deterministic policy gradients outperform the proposed method on specific metrics in selected environments. Ablation studies further show that expert-dataset diversity and rare-event coverage are essential for policy quality, while posterior-collapse diagnostics confirm that the learned latent representation remains informative throughout training. Overall, the proposed framework constitutes a competitive and computationally efficient alternative for offline energy management, particularly in settings where safe exploration, fast convergence, and degradation-aware control are more critical than unconstrained asymptotic performance.

papers.title: Integrating machine learning demand forecasting and adaptive operational control in inpatient stroke care: an analysis with real hospital data
papers.abstract: Objective: To compare capacity allocation policies for inpatient stroke care integrating Random Forest demand forecasting with machine-learning model predictive control (ML-MPC). Methods: Retrospective simulation study using 6,224 stroke admissions at a public neurological reference hospital in Southeastern Brazil (2006–2022). A daily series (2015–2022) was split into training (2015–2019), validation (2020) and test (2021–2022). Base capacity was derived from the 90th percentile of the observed daily census. Six policies were simulated over 727 days, with multi-step forecasts generated recursively from information available at each decision instant; uncertainty was assessed by moving-block bootstrap, re-executing all policies on resampled trajectories. Results: ML-MPC attained a mean simulated queue of 0.55 patients and the lowest objective-function value, 58% below the robust policy using 71% less extraordinary capacity (708 fewer units), and 46% below a naive fixed-capacity policy; 95% intervals excluded zero for blocks of 14, 30 and 60 days. Random Forest accuracy exceeded a historical-mean benchmark only marginally (MAE 0.994 vs 0.999). Conclusion: Within model conditions, how forecasts, uncertainty and capacity constraints entered sequential decisions mattered more than forecast accuracy. Outcomes are simulation estimates; no patient was exposed, the risk term is a non-validated relative index, and objective weights are judgment-based, not monetary.

papers.title: Systematic Uncertainty Below 10^-18 in the Aluminium Quantum-Logic Clock: Motion, Zeeman and Blackbody Budgets
papers.abstract: Systematic uncertainty below 10^-18 in the aluminium quantum-logic clock is examined for the NIST aluminium-27 quantum-logic clock, with a published systematic uncertainty of 9.4 parts inside 10^19, the smallest total reported for any clock in its era. Principal computed quantities: total uncertainty e19 = 9.462; published total e19 = 9.4; ratio computed to published = 1.007; motion pair e19 = 6.574; motion share of variance pct = 48.28; height equivalent mm = 8.671. The governing idea, for NIST aluminium-27 quantum-logic clock, runs as follows. A single trapped ion has no density shift and almost no blackbody shift, so its budget is dominated instead by motion: the time-dilation effects of secular motion and excess micromotion, and by the second-order zeeman shift of the trapping field. Setting total uncertainty e19 at 9.462 beside published total e19 at 9.4 shows, for NIST aluminium-27 quantum-logic clock, the scale, for NIST aluminium-27 quantum-logic clock, before interpretation. Both numbers, for NIST aluminium-27 quantum-logic clock, come from the systematic uncertainty below 10^-18 in the aluminium quantum-logic clock relations. The later discussion, for NIST aluminium-27 quantum-logic clock, sets total uncertainty e19 at 9.462 against published values for NIST aluminium-27 quantum-logic clock and names, for NIST aluminium-27 quantum-logic clock, the input moving total uncertainty e19 at 9.462 furthest.

papers.title: BALANCE-ST: distilling deep reinforcement learning policies into PLC logic for multi-VFD load balancing
papers.abstract: Industrial multi-VFD load balancing on programmable logic controllers (PLCs) requires control policies that are accurate, transparent, and fast enough for deterministic scan cycles. Deep reinforcement learning can learn effective balancing strategies, but neural policies are difficult to inspect and deploy as IEC 61131-3 Structured Text (ST). We propose BALANCE-ST, a simulation-to-PLC pipeline that trains a deep Q -network (DQN) teacher, distils it into a depth-2 decision tree selected by held-out validation parsimony, renders the tree as PLC-oriented ST, and wraps the resulting policy with a deterministic guard enforcing command-bound, ramp-rate, dwell-time, and overload checks. In an in-distribution post-training evaluation across eight demand families and ten seeds, BALANCE-ST achieves mean load-imbalance coefficient of variation 0.0697 versus 0.0696 for the ten-teacher DQN aggregate, while reducing imbalance by \(34.4\%\) , \(52.6\%\) , and \(15.0\%\) relative to equal-share, threshold-staging, and PI baselines, respectively. On the interquartile mean, the reduction versus threshold staging is \(43.2\%\) . A guard ablation and hard-stress evaluation show that the runtime guard reduces realised violations at the cost of higher imbalance under actuator dropout. Compared with beam-search model predictive control, BALANCE-ST yields higher imbalance but much lower online decision cost and a compact policy with four leaves and three effective actions. These results support BALANCE-ST as a practical trade-off between control performance, inspectability, and deployment-oriented simplicity for PLC-based multi-VFD control.

papers.title: Timed Elastic Band based trajectory planning and MPC based adaptive cruise control for car-like autonomous vehicle
papers.abstract: This paper presents a hierarchical control architecture for a car-like autonomous vehicle. Lateral motion is handled by a Timed Elastic Band (TEB) local planner that repeatedly optimizes a short-horizon waypoint band, while steering is generated by a Pure Pursuit controller tracking the optimized local path. Longitudinal behaviour is governed by a model predictive control (MPC) based adaptive cruise control (ACC) that regulates speed and inter-vehicle distance in free-driving and car-following modes, explicitly respecting acceleration and braking limits and enforcing a minimum safety distance. Safety is addressed through constraint-aware planning and control: the TEB optimization penalizes proximity to obstacles and violations of lane boundaries using smooth penalty terms that support stable gradient-based updates, while the MPC-ACC embeds hard bounds and distance constraints to prevent unsafe following. The integrated stack is evaluated in representative driving scenarios, including lane keeping and car-following, and is benchmarked against the MathWorks Path Following Control System (PFCS) reference model to quantify tracking behaviour and constraint compliance under identical conditions.
